latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n > 1, a real number x, and an integer m. By the definition of E_n,

E_n(x+m) = floor(n(x+m)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+m))/k.

Since m is an integer, nm is an integer and km is an integer for every integer k. Therefore, using floor(t+z)=floor(t)+z whenever z is an integer,

floor(n(x+m)) = floor(nx+nm) = floor(nx) + nm,

and for each k = 1, ..., n,

floor(k(x+m)) = floor(kx+km) = floor(kx) + km.

Hence

floor(k(x+m))/k = floor(kx)/k + m.

Substituting these identities into the definition gives

E_n(x+m) = (floor(nx)+nm) - sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)/k + m).

Because there are n terms in the sum,

E_n(x+m) = floor(nx) + nm - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k - nm = E_n(x).

Thus E_n(x+m) = E_n(x) for every real x and every integer m.
